title_en: Liu Meifang v. Changzhou Kairui Chemical Technology Co., Ltd., et al. — dispute over confirmation of the validity of corporate resolutions
ruling_gist_en: Where a shareholder of a limited liability company fails to perform the capital contribution obligation or withdraws all capital contributions, and after the company urges the shareholder to make or return the capital contributions, the shareholder still fails to do so within a reasonable period, the company may, by a resolution of the shareholders' meeting, remove the shareholder's qualification. However, if all shareholders of the company have made false capital contributions or withdrawn all capital contributions, and some shareholders resolve to remove the qualification of a specific shareholder through a shareholders' meeting resolution, because such shareholders themselves are not honest and compliant shareholders, the exercise of their voting rights for expulsion lacks a legitimate basis, and such expulsion resolution shall be deemed invalid.
keywords_en: Civil; Dispute over confirmation of validity of company resolution; Second instance; Intermediate People's Court; Jiangsu Province; Natural person; Legal person; Company Law; Validity of shareholder expulsion resolution; Determination of withdrawal of capital contributions; Legitimacy of shareholders' voting rights; Reversal of judgment; Shareholder expulsion; Withdrawal of capital contributions; Dispute between husband-and-wife shareholders; Good faith; Company and other disputes over confirmation of validity of company resolution
full_text_en:
Liu Meifang v. Changzhou Kairui Chemical Technology Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over confirmation of validity of company resolution

【Ruling Summary】

Where a shareholder of a limited liability company fails to perform its capital contribution obligation or withdraws all of its capital contribution, and after the company issues a demand for contribution or return, the shareholder still fails to make contribution or return within a reasonable period, the company may remove the shareholder's status by means of a shareholders' resolution. However, if all shareholders of the company have made false capital contributions or withdrawn all capital contributions, and some shareholders, by means of a shareholders' resolution, remove the shareholder status of a specific shareholder, such shareholders themselves are not shareholders acting in good faith and observing the agreement, and thus the legal basis for exercising the voting right of expulsion is lost, and such expulsion resolution shall be determined as invalid.

Plaintiff: Liu Meifang, female, Han ethnicity, born on December 10, 1979, residing in Nantong City, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Changzhou Kairui Chemical Technology Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Times Square, Zouqu Town, Zhonglou District, Changzhou City, Jiangsu Province.

Third Party: Hong Qiang, male, Han ethnicity, born on December 4, 1980, residing in Nantong City, Jiangsu Province.

Third Party: Hong Angang, male, Han ethnicity, born on December 29, 1972, residing in Taihe County, Anhui Province.

Plaintiff Liu Meifang brought an action before the Zhonglou District People's Court of Changzhou City, Jiangsu Province, against Defendant Changzhou Kairui Chemical Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kairui Company) and Third Parties Hong Qiang and Hong Angang concerning a dispute over confirmation of validity of company resolution.

Plaintiff Liu Meifang alleged: On November 20, 2017, shareholders Hong Qiang and Hong Angang of Defendant Kairui Company convened a shareholders' meeting and passed a resolution to remove Liu Meifang's shareholder status on the ground that Liu Meifang had withdrawn all capital contributions and failed to repay within a reasonable period after demand. After the resolution was made, it was not notified to the plaintiff until December 21, 2017 (the day before the trial of the lawsuit between the plaintiff and the defendant concerning the right to know), when Kairui Company, in its defense, claimed that the plaintiff's shareholder status had been removed by this resolution. It was then that the plaintiff learned of the content of the shareholders' resolution. This shareholders' resolution removing the plaintiff's shareholder status is invalid because it violates the law. First, at the time of establishment of Kairui Company, all shareholders including the plaintiff had actually paid in the registered capital of RMB 510,000 on July 7, 2009, as verified by a capital verification report issued by Changzhou Fangzheng Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd.; on February 6, 2015, Kairui Company increased its registered capital to RMB 3,000,000 and amended its articles of association, and after the increase, the plaintiff actually contributed RMB 1,350,000, which has been fully paid. The subscription period actually stipulated in Kairui Company's articles of association is December 31, 2018, and the plaintiff does not fall under the circumstances of withdrawal of registered capital as provided by law. Second, Kairui Company's claim that the plaintiff withdrew all registered capital and misappropriated company property has no factual basis and legal basis. Although Kairui Company had sued the plaintiff in court on the ground of liability for damages to company interests, there has been no final judgment characterizing the so-called transferred funds referred to by Kairui Company. The "Other Accounts Payable Subsidiary Ledger" provided by the plaintiff in that case is sufficient to prove that the plaintiff did not withdraw registered capital or misappropriate company property, but that Kairui Company repaid personal loans to the plaintiff, which Kairui Company was aware of and approved of, and which had been recorded in the accounts. Therefore, a transfer from Kairui Company's bank account does not necessarily mean that registered capital was withdrawn or company property was misappropriated. The plaintiff prayed for a judgment: 1. confirming that the shareholders' resolution made by Kairui Company on November 20, 2017 to remove the plaintiff's shareholder status is invalid; 2. ordering Kairui Company to bear the litigation costs of this case.

Defendant Kairui Company argued: The plaintiff Liu Meifang, as a shareholder of the company, withdrew all capital contributions and misappropriated part of the company's assets during the normal operation of the company. The facts are clear and the evidence is sufficient. The shareholders' resolution made on November 20, 2017 by the shareholders of Kairui Company, namely Third Parties Hong Qiang and Hong Angang, to remove the plaintiff's shareholder status for the protection of their legitimate rights and interests and the normal operation of the company is lawful and valid. The defendant requests the court to reject the plaintiff's claims according to law.

Third Parties Hong Qiang and Hong Angang argued in agreement with the defense of Defendant Kairui Company.

The Zhonglou District People's Court of Changzhou City, Jiangsu Province found at first instance:

Defendant Kairui Company was established on July 10, 2009, with a business scope including wholesale of hazardous chemicals, research and development of chemical auxiliaries, technology transfer and technical services; sales of non-hazardous chemical raw materials and products; self-operated or agency import and export of various goods and technologies (except for goods and technologies restricted or prohibited by the state from being operated or imported/exported by enterprises), and other business activities permitted after approval by relevant authorities according to law. The amended articles of association of Kairui Company dated February 2015 recorded: The registered capital of Kairui Company is RMB 3,000,000, with shareholders including Liu Meifang, Hong Angang, and Hong Qiang, among whom Liu Meifang and Hong Qiang each contributed RMB 1,350,000, and Hong Angang contributed RMB 300,000. Of Liu Meifang's contribution, RMB 229,500 was paid on July 7, 2009, and RMB 1,120,500 was to be paid before December 30, 2018 (capital increase).

Plaintiff Liu Meifang and Third Party Hong Qiang were formerly husband and wife. In March 2016, Liu Meifang filed a divorce lawsuit against Hong Qiang, which was accepted by the court of first instance. In the complaint, Liu Meifang stated: "In February 2016, the conflict between the two parties further intensified. The defendant suddenly took away all the company seal and financial seal needed for the operation of Kairui Company. To prevent the defendant from transferring the funds in Kairui Company's account, the plaintiff transferred most of the funds in Kairui Company's account to her own account to secure the safety of the funds."

On September 21, 2017, the court of first instance accepted the case of Kairui Company v. Liu Meifang and Changzhou Nuowei'er Chemical Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Nuowei'er Company) concerning a dispute over liability for damages to company interests, i.e., Case No. (2017) Su 0404 Min Chu 5248. In that case, Kairui Company demanded that Liu Meifang return RMB 2,951,420.9 plus interest, and that Nuowei'er Company bear joint and several liability for RMB 1,095,000 of that amount. During the trial of that case, Kairui Company clarified that the claimed RMB 2,951,420.9 consisted of two parts: RMB 1,350,000 being the full amount of Liu Meifang's withdrawn capital contribution, and RMB 1,601,420.9 being misappropriated company funds. After Kairui Company filed the lawsuit, Liu Meifang did not return the funds to Kairui Company. On October 31 of the same year, Kairui Company notified Liu Meifang in writing of the convening of an extraordinary shareholders' meeting for 2017, scheduled for 3:00 p.m. on November 20, 2017. The agenda was to consider and vote on the expulsion of the shareholder Liu Meifang on the ground that she had withdrawn all capital contributions and had not returned them within a reasonable period after the company's demand. On November 7 of the same year, Liu Meifang replied by letter that the agenda of the extraordinary shareholders' meeting violated legal provisions and lacked basis. On November 20 of the same year, Kairui Company held a shareholders' meeting and adopted a shareholders' resolution. The shareholders present were Hong Qiang and Hong Angang. The shareholders' resolution recorded: Whereas shareholder Liu Meifang, in the course of the company's operations, has taken advantage of her position to withdraw all capital contributions and misappropriate company property, and after the company's demand, has still not repaid within a reasonable period, the members present at the shareholders' meeting unanimously voted to remove Liu Meifang's shareholder status, and the company will assist with relevant registration changes thereafter.

Separately, on November 6 of the same year, Plaintiff Liu Meifang sent a request for inspection to Defendant Kairui Company, requesting to inspect the accounting financial reports, accounting books, and original accounting vouchers of Kairui Company from 2009 to the first three quarters of 2017. On December 5, 2017, Liu Meifang filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance to exercise her shareholder's right to know and to inspect relevant financial vouchers of Kairui Company. On December 22, 2017, the court of first instance issued Civil Ruling (2017) Su 0404 Min Chu 6534, dismissing Liu Meifang's lawsuit. During the trial of that case, Kairui Company stated that, given that Liu Meifang's shareholder status had been removed, Kairui Company amended its claims in Case No. (2017) Su 0404 Min Chu 5248 and no longer demanded that Liu Meifang return the capital contribution of RMB 1,350,000.

The Zhonglou District People's Court of Changzhou City, Jiangsu Province reasoned at first instance:

According to relevant legal provisions, where a shareholder of a limited liability company fails to perform its capital contribution obligation or withdraws all capital contributions, and after the company issues a demand for contribution or return, the shareholder still fails to make contribution or return within a reasonable period, and the company removes the shareholder's status by means of a shareholders' resolution, and the shareholder requests a confirmation that the removal is invalid, the people's court shall not support such request. In March 2016, Liu Meifang filed a divorce lawsuit against Hong Qiang, which was accepted by the court of first instance. In the complaint in the divorce case filed in March 2016, Liu Meifang stated: "In February 2016, she transferred most of the funds in Kairui Company's account to her own account to secure the safety of the funds." In September 2017, Kairui Company filed a lawsuit demanding that Liu Meifang return RMB 2,951,420.9, including the full amount of Liu Meifang's capital contribution of RMB 1,350,000. This lawsuit constituted a demand by Kairui Company to Liu Meifang. However, Liu Meifang did not return the capital contribution within a reasonable period. Therefore, Kairui Company sent a notice to Liu Meifang convening a shareholders' meeting, fulfilled the notification obligation, and held the shareholders' meeting on schedule to adopt the resolution. The content of this resolution does not violate legal provisions. Liu Meifang's request to confirm the resolution as invalid lacks legal basis and is not supported.

Accordingly, in accordance with Article 17 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (III), the Zhonglou District People's Court of Changzhou City, Jiangsu Province, on March 7, 2018, rendered the following judgment:

Reject Plaintiff Liu Meifang's claims.

The case acceptance fee is reduced by half to RMB 40, to be borne by Plaintiff Liu Meifang.

Liu Meifang, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Intermediate People's Court of Changzhou City, Jiangsu Province, alleging: First, the court of first instance, relying solely on the statements made by Liu Meifang's former agent ad litem in Case No. (2016) Su 0404 Min Chu 1221, without examining the accounting books and vouchers of Kairui Company, concluded that Liu Meifang had admitted to withdrawing all capital contributions of RMB 1,350,000, and applied Article 17 of the Judicial Interpretation (III) of the Company Law to dismiss Liu Meifang's request to confirm the invalidity of the shareholders' resolution. This constitutes an error in fact-finding and application of law. 1. The "Other Accounts Payable Subsidiary Ledger" for the period from January 2015 to December 2016 provided to Liu Meifang by the accountant of Changzhou Jinxin Accounting Consulting Service Co., Ltd., engaged by Kairui Company, is sufficient to prove that the funds in question were loans repaid by Kairui Company to Liu Meifang personally and had been recorded in the company's accounts. The transfer of these funds was an act of Kairui Company, not a personal act of Liu Meifang. The true nature of the funds cannot be determined merely from a bank transaction record. 2. The statements made by Liu Meifang's former agent ad litem in Case No. (2016) Su 0404 Min Chu 1221 were not Liu Meifang's own opinion, and the company's account records better reflect the facts of this case. To ascertain the facts, the appellant requests the court of second instance to order Kairui Company to produce all of its accounting books, original accounting vouchers, and financial accounting reports from its establishment on July 10, 2009 to the present. Second, the court of first instance did not fully find the facts. Liu Meifang, Hong Qiang, and Hong Angang all failed to make capital contributions, so there is no fact that Liu Meifang withdrew capital contributions, and Hong Qiang and Hong Angang have no right to adopt a resolution to remove Liu Meifang's shareholder status. Third, Kairui Company's financial accounts are divided into five parts: 1. The publicly disclosed accounts prepared by the accountant of Changzhou Jinxin Accounting Consulting Service Co., Ltd.; 2. Transactions of Hong Angang's accounts ending in 6070 at the Agricultural Bank of China Changzhou Zhonglou Development Zone Sub-branch and ending in 3519 at the Agricultural Bank of China Yonghong Sub-branch; 3. Transactions of Liu Meifang's accounts ending in 1679 and 5911 at the Agricultural Bank of China Changzhou Zhonglou Sub-branch; 4. Transactions of Hong Qiang's account ending in 4416 at the Agricultural Bank of China Dushi Taoyuan Sub-branch and transactions on the WeChat account starting with HQ. The difference in usage of the above accounts is that most transactions requiring invoices were conducted through the accounts of Changzhou Jinxin Accounting Consulting Service Co., Ltd. The funds that Kairui Company transferred into Liu Meifang's above accounts still belonged to the company, and similarly, company funds were also transferred into the above accounts of Hong Angang and Hong Qiang. For example, in the divorce proceedings between Liu Meifang and Hong Qiang, the RMB 1,050,000 paid by Hong Qiang to Liu Meifang originated from the company's account. In summary, the appellant requests the court of second instance to ascertain the facts and amend the judgment to support all of Liu Meifang's claims.

Appellee Kairui Company argued: The first-instance judgment correctly found the facts with sufficient evidence, and the appellee requests the court of second instance to affirm it. Even if, at present, the second-phase capital increase of all three shareholders has not yet become due and Article 17 of the Judicial Interpretation (III) of the Company Law is not applicable, Appellant Liu Meifang should still make the capital contribution within that period, i.e., after December 30, 2018, the company will continue to demand payment from Liu Meifang. If Liu Meifang believes that she still has shareholder status, she should assume the obligation to pay.

Third Parties at first instance Hong Qiang and Hong Angang argued in agreement with the above opinion of Appellee Kairui Company.

The Intermediate People's Court of Changzhou City, Jiangsu Province, after the second-instance trial, confirmed the facts found at first instance.

Separately found: The content of the articles of association of Appellee Kairui Company dated February 2015 does not fully correspond to the actual situation. The registered capital of Kairui Company at the time of its establishment was RMB 510,000. Third Party at first instance Hong Qiang and Appellant Liu Meifang each contributed RMB 229,500, and Third Party at first instance Hong Angang contributed RMB 51,000, but none of them made actual capital contributions. In February 2015, the registered capital of Kairui Company was increased to RMB 3,000,000. Hong Qiang and Liu Meifang each increased their contributions by RMB 1,120,500, and Hong Angang increased his contribution by RMB 249,000, all of which were to be fully paid by December 30, 2018.

The Intermediate People's Court of Changzhou City, Jiangsu Province reasoned at second instance:

The issue in dispute in this case is: How should the validity of the shareholders' resolution for expulsion at issue be determined?

The court holds that the adoption and content of the shareholders' resolution for expulsion in this case lack legal basis and factual support and should be held invalid. On the one hand, based on an analysis of the legal basis and function of the right of expulsion, a company is a contractual combination formed among shareholders, between shareholders and the company, and between the company and the government. Therefore, the relationship among shareholders is naturally bound by that contract. Throughout the existence of the company, shareholders must always faithfully and actually perform their capital contribution obligations. Failure to do so constitutes a breach of the reasonable expectations of other shareholders who comply with the contract and thus a breach of the corporate contract. Once a shareholder fails to perform its capital contribution obligation or withdraws all capital contributions, such a breach seriously jeopardizes the company's operations and the common interests of the other shareholders, deviating from the purpose and original intent of the contract. Therefore, the Company Law grants the shareholders who comply with the contract the right to terminate the contractual relationship among themselves and to cause the breaching shareholder to withdraw from the company. This reflects both the law's punishment and sanction against the breaching party and its relief and protection for the complying party. It follows that the right to "terminate" (a contract or shareholder status) vests only in the complying party; the breaching party does not enjoy such right. In this case, all shareholders of Appellee Kairui Company, at the time of the company's establishment, acted with collusive intent, made false capital contributions, and maliciously infringed upon the rights and interests of the company and its creditors. However, within the shareholder group itself, there is no so-called impairment of legitimate rights and interests, and thus no basis for relief. Otherwise, it would contravene legal principles such as the conformity of rights and obligations and fairness and good faith. That is to say, Third Parties at first instance Hong Qiang and Hong Angang have no right to resolve to expel Appellant Liu Meifang's shareholder status by convening a shareholders' meeting; the initiation of the expulsion resolution is clearly unlawful. On the other hand, from the distinction between false capital contribution and withdrawal of capital contribution: the former refers to a shareholder's failure to perform or fully perform the capital contribution obligation, while the latter refers to a shareholder taking back the contribution after having performed it. The shareholders' resolution for expulsion in this case determined that Liu Meifang had withdrawn all capital contributions. In fact, all shareholders of Kairui Company, including Liu Meifang, failed to perform their capital contribution obligations at the time of the company's establishment, constituting false capital contributions. Therefore, the content determined by the resolution also contradicts the objective facts.

In summary, Appellant Liu Meifang's ground of appeal that Third Parties at first instance Hong Qiang and Hong Angang had no right to adopt the expulsion resolution is well-founded and should be supported. The court of first instance incorrectly found the facts and misapplied the law, which should be corrected. In accordance with Article 22 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and Item 2 of Paragraph 1 of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Intermediate People's Court of Changzhou City, Jiangsu Province, on August 2, 2018, rendered the following judgment:

1. Reverse the Civil Judgment (2018) Su 0404 Min Chu 515 of the Zhonglou District People's Court of Changzhou City, Jiangsu Province;

2. The shareholders' resolution of Changzhou Kairui Chemical Technology Co., Ltd. made on November 20, 2017 to remove Liu Meifang's shareholder status is invalid.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 40 and the second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 80 shall be borne by Kairui Company.

This judgment is final.
